column1: # Wide-cite audit, 2026-11-14. Written by DeepSeek for Zach's overnight list. Do not edit by hand.

# Question: for act.informative.c and act.wizard.c, which depth-manifest rows are "covered" only by a C citation range wider than 20 lines, and does the retained C transcript of the scenario the row names actually print text from that range?

# Frame: docs/fidelity/depth/*.tsv at origin/main 90c3c6b58, rows with status oracle-green*. A row is in frame when EVERY citation of that file in its c_site is a range longer than 20 lines; single-line and <=20-line citations are out of frame.

# Evidence: retained seed-1 C blocks from /home/zach/Archives/darkpawns/oracle-runs/2026-11-13/hydrogen-dp1477-combined/census-dump (go-head 16bef904f; full corpus, 1,879 scenarios). The C blocks are engine-side and seed-deterministic, so this dump remains valid evidence at later Go heads; every cited line was re-read against src/ at 90c3c6b58.

# Test: for each in-frame row, every C string literal in the cited lines with at least 8 characters of fixed text (format specifiers removed) is a candidate. Each candidate is searched in the scenario's normalized C blocks, ANSI stripped, with whitespace-tolerant matching. Verdict:
#   witnessed     = at least one candidate literal appears in C's blocks
#   not-witnessed = at least one candidate exists and none appears

#   cant-tell     = no retained block, every block empty, no candidate literal in the range, or the only candidates belong to a class the normalizer erases or masks (version/build stamp, uptime, wall clock, player counts)

# Limitation: witnessed is an any-literal test. A wide range that prints its header and none of its branches still counts. literals_found/literals_total is the strength column: under 25% means the transcript touched the range, not the row's claim.

# Counts: 280 rows in frame (act.wizard.c 163, act.informative.c 117): witnessed 202, not-witnessed 53, cant-tell 25. By file: act.wizard.c 147/13/3, act.informative.c 55/40/22. Of the 202 witnessed rows, 54 matched under 25% of their candidates, 75 between 25% and 50%, 47 between 50% and 75%, and 26 at 75% or more.
